title: the departure
hook: before he leaves, Rama gives everything away, and makes a poor old man throw his stick

segments.voice: Yesterday: Urmila, left in Valmiki's silence, and Lakshmana's anger given work: a bow, a spade and a basket. Today the departure begins, with giving.
screen: `A BOW, A SPADE AND A BASKET.`

segments.voice: Armlets. Earrings. A golden girdle. A herd of cows. On the day Rama leaves, his rooms empty out, piece by piece, into other people's hands. Leaving a home can come with a day like this, sad and oddly freeing at once: the couch to a cousin, the plants to whoever will water them. Here it's a prince's wealth. And in the middle of it, Valmiki tells a small story with a joke in it, on a day built for tears.
screen: `ARMLETS, EARRINGS, COWS.` → `A PRINCE'S WEALTH, GIVEN AWAY.` → `A JOKE ON A DAY OF TEARS.`

segments.voice: Rama sends for Suyajna, the son of his teacher Vasishtha, and gives him armlets, earrings and jewels. Sita sends a necklace and a golden girdle to Suyajna's wife. Gifts go to teachers, to the brahmins who taught the princes, to old household servants, to everyone who depends on Rama for a living, so no one is left without support while he's gone. Then the story. Near Ayodhya lives a very poor brahmin named Trijata, old and thin, who scrapes a living digging in the fields with a spade. His wife hears Rama is giving things away. Go, she says. Maybe he'll give you something. So Trijata stands before the prince, and Rama, of all things, teases him. I haven't yet given away even a thousand of my cows. Throw your staff. However far it lands, every cow up to that point is yours. The old man ties up his clothes, swings with every bit of strength he has, and throws. The staff flies across the river Sarayu and lands in a pasture full of cattle. Rama embraces him and gives him every cow up to that spot. Then he apologizes. Don't be offended. It was a joke. I only wanted to see the strength in you. A tiny scene, but look at what it shows. On the day his life is falling apart, Rama is still generous, still playful, still minding one poor man's dignity. Grief hasn't made him small.
screen: `GIFTS SO NO ONE IS LEFT WITHOUT.` · `TRIJATA, OLD, POOR, WITH A SPADE.` · `THROW YOUR STAFF.` · `IT WAS A JOKE. FORGIVE ME.` · then, large: `GRIEF HASN'T MADE HIM SMALL.`

segments.voice: Look around in your mind at what you own, and pick one thing someone else would use. Picture handing it over, and notice how it feels to let it go. Then rest in the breath, lighter by one thing.
The departure, part one: giving. Rama and Sita give away their wealth, and Rama makes poor Trijata throw his staff, and gives him every cow up to where it lands.
Your line: throw your staff. Even on his hardest day, Rama gives with a smile. That's day five hundred thirty-one.

howItsDone: Hindus give dana, gifts, at turning points such as rites, festivals and journeys; in the text, Rama gives before he leaves, and the Trijata episode is a light moment in a dark book.

fork.setup: you're Trijata, old and poor. a prince tells you to throw your staff: every cow up to where it lands is yours. what do you do?
options: toss it politely a few feet.
tie up your clothes and throw with all your strength.
fork.reveal: he throws with everything he has, the staff flies across the Sarayu, and Rama gives him the cows, then apologizes for the joke.

original.note: Sanskrit dāna: giving, a gift; what Rama and Sita do with their wealth before they leave.

trapdoor: what you thought: the departure is all tears.
what it means: it begins with generous giving, and even a joke.
what a scholar hears: it's a comic moment in a grieving book, and it shows that Valmiki's Rama can tease, and apologize.

chat.says: Rama's being exiled and he's cracking jokes? Isn't that strange?
options: He gives generously, teases an old man, then apologizes. Grief hasn't made him small.
He jokes because he doesn't believe the exile is real yet, so nothing feels sad.
He's mocking Trijata, and Valmiki shows it as a cruel moment for the prince.
chat.meaning: Rama teases Trijata, gives him the cows, and apologizes. On the day his life falls apart, he's still generous and kind.
